To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Sleeping Beauty transposase-mediated germline integration of a Venus reporter transgene in rabbits and mice resulted in a differential reporter expression in mature spermatozoon, which is likely due to intercellular bridge formation during spermatogenesis.
the Venus reporter is expressed in spermatids of rabbits, and not in mice, suggesting that intercellular bridges are present in rabbits and not mice.

the Venus transgene is expressed in a species-specific manner in spermatids of mice and rabbits, and that this differential expression is likely to result from differences in the structure of the intercellular bridges that link developing germ cells.

the generation of transgenic rabbit lines for functional studies of male fertility, and the development of a new rabbit model for male infertility.
the development of transgenic rabbit lines for biomedical research, in which transposon-mediated germline gene transfer was applied.
the development and application of transgenic rabbit lines and their comparison with transgenic mice.

the Venus reporter is expressed in the intercellular bridges of the male rabbit germline.
the Venus reporter protein is not expressed in mature spermatozoon of the mouse and rabbit.
the Venus reporter protein is present in the intercellular bridges of spermatids of the rabbit, whereas it is absent from intercellular bridges and sperm heads of the mouse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Venus rabbit reporter line is a valuable tool for functional analysis of testicular development and male infertility in men.
the transgenic rabbit model provides a unique opportunity to investigate the male germlines and to identify novel genes involved in testicular development.
the Venus reporter is expressed in the cytoplasm of the spermatid nucleus and is not transferred to the sperm head during spermatozoa maturation.

the Venus reporter protein is expressed in mature rabbit spermatids, whereas in mouse spermatids the Venus protein is not detectable.
